repository.name: jobFynder-BE-nestJS
repository.description: This is for BE rewamp to nestJS from nodeJS

commits.message:
fix(ai): route all AI calls through LiteLLM, remove Portkey and direct OpenAI

CORE previously had two separate ways of reaching a model provider,
neither of which was LiteLLM: AiService wrapped Portkey directly
(new Portkey({apiKey, baseURL})), and resume.controller.ts held a
second, completely separate direct OpenAI client
(new OpenAI({apiKey: openaiApiKey})) used by the generate-section
endpoint, bypassing even Portkey. Per the platform-wide rule
(LiteLLM is the sole AI gateway -- no service may call a model
provider or an intermediate gateway directly), both are now OpenAI
SDK clients pointed at gateway.jobfynder.com with a LiteLLM virtual
key, since LiteLLM exposes an OpenAI-compatible API.

Also fixed four hardcoded, Portkey-specific model routing strings
that would not have resolved against LiteLLM
(@chatgpt/gpt-4o-mini, @chatgpt/gpt-4.1-mini x2, @grok/llama-3.1-8b-instant,
plus the gpt-4-0125-preview/gpt-3.5-turbo two-tier fallback in
generate-section) -- all now use LiteLLM router aliases
(generate-small, extract-fast) matching what Hermes itself uses,
so model/provider selection is centralized at the gateway instead
of hardcoded per caller. The two-tier client-side fallback in
generate-section is removed since LiteLLM handles fallback at the
gateway level now.

configuration.ts/env.validation.ts: added LITELLM_API_KEY/
LITELLM_BASE_URL (optional, matching the existing pattern).
PORTKEY_API_KEY/PORTKEY_BASE_URL/OPENAI_API_KEY left in place but
unused, so a deployment that still has them set does not fail
validation -- true removal is a follow-up cleanup, not required for
this fix.

Verified: npm run build clean, pm2 restart --update-env, live
end-to-end call against the exact new config (LITELLM_API_KEY/
LITELLM_BASE_URL from .env) through the generate-small alias
succeeded. grep -rn portkey/OpenAI-direct-usage across src/ confirms
zero remaining Portkey references and both OpenAI() instantiations
now point at LiteLLM.

Does not yet address the deeper architectural gap (CORE should
ideally call Hermes's existing HERMES-200/HERMES-800 endpoints for
resume parsing/generation instead of any LLM gateway directly --
two of these four call sites map closely onto capabilities Hermes
already has, tagged and RBAC-protected). Tracked as a separate,
larger follow-up; this fix closes the immediate HERMES-1000 exit
condition (no direct provider/Portkey calls anywhere in the
platform) without touching response shapes or risking the live
resume-upload/content-generation UX.
